program: Public-benefit enrollment, insurance navigation and benefit literacy
priceScope: Historical full annual recipient cost against conditional current navigation benefits; not a matched current whole-portfolio or marginal-gift EV.

what: Benefits in Action assists with SNAP, health insurance, disability and other public-benefit applications.
Its food-delivery program ended April30,2026; current navigation continues statewide.
A conditional health-plus-net-transfer reference is about $14.3M per better life.
strengths: Current recipient sources identify free application assistance and dated food-program closure.
Original filings and legal donor identity were independently checked.
The calculation includes recipient resources, full participation burdens and distinct public-payer losses.
reservations: Individuals and families are mixed units; applications are not unique approvals or causal outcomes.
Historical expenses include discontinued food delivery and are not a current navigation budget.
Incremental enrollment, household benefit amounts, health utility and local share remain hypotheses.

sections.what: Benefits in Action, EIN87-3774775, offers free application assistance, benefit literacy and referral support. SNAP, Medicare, Medicaid, Connect for Health Colorado, Social Security and LEAP are mechanisms, not measured new income. Official donation page names the legal payee/check route and links ColoradoGives; no transaction made. Food delivery ended April30,2026, despite stale donor-profile food wording.
sections.monitoring: The homepage2025 envelope is16000 individuals and families and28000 applications. These are mixed units and overlapping applications, not unique households or approvals. Its87% Medicaid enrollment/fewer-emergency-visits statement is descriptive, not a controlled causal coefficient. Request distinct current households, approvals versus alternative application, benefit duration, service county, after-tax/other-benefit-withdrawal resources and payer costs. Cumulative75000 since2015 is not annual output.
sections.qualitative: Enrollment may improve access to care and constrained household consumption, but self-application, county agencies, insurers and other navigators are alternatives. Model16000 mixed units times.5 household conversion; .2 incremental access, .2 health-compatible share, .3 clinical response and .01 utility for one year are explicit judgments. No ER reduction or avoided-death coefficient is imported. Current statewide navigation differs from the former four-county food service.
sections.cost: Original full FY2024 expenses $4,368,504 include $8,972 netted direct event costs. FY2023 full $2,525,910; two comparable full-year mean $3,447,207. FY2022 covered only July–December: $770,665 including $13,412 direct events, excluded from annual mean and not annualized. FY2024 $3,853,488 recognized program cost combines navigation and then-food work; it is only a historical mixed-program sensitivity, not allocated current navigation or a marginal donation price. Cost/output/program vintages do not match, so this is a conditional partial reference.
sections.funding: Judged$2400 annual resources for half of incremental households are actual disposable food/cash/utility benefits net of taxes, offsets and other benefit withdrawal, not insurance retail spending or gross wages. Positive gain is overlap-adjusted. Full$25 time/access costs and stress apply to all exposed households even failed applications. Same household benefit and costs share one log. Distinct taxpayer households lose full$2400 per changed household, without positive-overlap discount; local incidence applied once. Taxpayer baseline/group size and net benefit amounts are judgments. Insurance clinical access and consumption savings are not duplicated; additional public treatment/provider costs are adverse sensitivities. Next-gift capacity after food closure unknown.

model.costScope: Historical whole FY2024 annual entity expense with current navigation-only benefit hypothesis; no claim current budget, all-portfolio EV or next-gift offer.
model.geographicAttribution: Statewide navigation and Colorado Springs co-locations; g.6 judged beneficiary share in ten-county Denver CBSA19740. Former Jefferson/Denver/Adams/Arapahoe food footprint is not current navigation share.
model.formula: Health = N × unique × b × eligible × completion × response × q × finite discounted T × g minus full exposed harms. Same-household net resources including access costs are joint logged; distinct government payer loses full transferred resources localized once. Price=10C/(health + signed income equivalents) when positive.
model.counterfactual: Public self-application, county eligibility offices, insurer assistance and other navigators without this recipient; approved benefit may have arrived anyway.
model.attribution: Incremental benefit access b.2 is distinct from health eligibility/clinical response and resource recipient fraction. Enrollment and submitted applications are not additionality.
model.uncertainty: Finite one-year conditional reference, no local controlled health or disposable-income effect. Current unique cohort/budget and approval additionality unknown; food closure breaks portfolio comparability.
model.nativeOutcomes: 2025 mixed16000 individuals/families and28000 applications;87% Medicaid descriptive statement; current fooddelivery ceased2026. No counts converted to deaths prevented, completed treatments or net income automatically.
